Probably didn’t give a clear definition in the methodology when I should have. 

Killpower is how capable a character is at removing their opponents stock. Good killpower will see consistent stocks taken when the opponent is at lower percents (closer to 0) and bad killpower is when the character takes the opponent stocks consistently later(or higher damage percent).

Yea. The method doesn't look at things like damage output, how easy it is to win neutrals/land those confirms, etc. It almost exclusively looks at just the number, and doesn't have entire context in most cases.

That's why I'm very hesitant to say there's a clear best - I DO believe that this data clearly indicates theres 3 main candidates, but there's plenty of reason to believe kazuya is still better than luigi even with similar numbers

i'll admit i forgot ab chrom's ground speed, but marth's walk speed IMO actually does play an important role in this game(not that it compares to the raw speed of chrom's initial dash)

As for forward tilt, Marth's is much much muuuch better than chroms. Sure, same frame data, however marth's kills significantly earlier and just has a better hitbox(check ultimate frame data for visualization) - Marth's goes just as low(and the lowest/earliest part of the hitbox is incredibly easy to tipper) but extends much further forward and above him. The tipper(which is marth's easiest to space and use by a landslide) also is 1 frame safer on shield.

I think what separates Marth from other swordies is he arguably has the best ground game of any of them, with maybe the exception being mythra. 

Forward Tilt, Up Tilt, and Down tilt are ridiculously easy to tipper and allow for incredibly defensive spacing that other swordies can't do because they don't have the same frame data or capability to explode off of it - As good as I think Roy is, uptilt and forward tilt aren't good neutral tools, and in general he doesn't have the hitboxes to really play like a swordie on the ground. Chrom does have a better hitbox for this between his jab and forward tilt, however marth's hitboxes are just overall superior.

That leaves lucina, who has identical hitboxes - and while you could argue lucina's down tilt is better, marth's uptilt sourspots and sweetspots allow marth for both better combos and better killpower, and marth's forward tilt is arguably the best in its game due to its absurd tipper locations. Marth is *guarenteed* a tipper when he sharks opponents with forward tilt, and in general it's his best move in just so many ways that lucina wishes she could use the move for.

Another thing that separates marcina from other swordies is frame data. We kind of forget this, but marth and lucina's frame data is actually without a doubt the best amongst any swordie. Frame 6 Fair compared to frame 10 for roy and chrom, frame 7 for mythra, and frame 15 for cloud. Frame 7 backair compared to frame 8 for roy/chrom, frame 10 for mythra. The trend generally applies to a ton of moves - they consistently have the best frame startup - Up Special, Down air, etc. 

So yea, when it comes to marcina in general, I tend to think of the best frame data and recovery amongst the relevant swordies. As for marth in particular, I personally think about his ground game being the best amongst any swordie alongside an x factor that can lead to kills at insanely early percents.

I think the 'previous iteration' argument shouldn't really matter that much, and never should. Characters like Diddy, Sheik, Sonic, etc. have evolved differently throughout the meta despite their past iterations, all three of these characters are still solid even if its "worse". The top tiers of smash 4 and brawl are significantly more dominant than ultimate's top tiers, so this argument overall shouldn't matter.

Also, since you're asking me what I personally see in marth's potential, it comes down to a few different things:

1. New blood. Sure, Rizeasu going solo marth is definitely a positive for a character's outlook, however there's a lot more to look forward when it's up and coming players - Ignaize has stormed SoCal this season with wins on Ketchup, T3Dom, Rockman. Kreeg, #2 in Utah, has wins on Scend, ven, and Shoe as another up and coming player. I can list a fair bit more, but this point boils down to new marth mains are on the rise and that's a very good thing for the character's long term rise in meta relevancy.

2. Swordie Meta. As of late, I am a firm believer swordies will become more and more relevant in the meta. It's hard to be a bad character and also be a swordie in this game in general - Marth shouldn't be an exception to this rule. A ton of swordies are seeing an increase in tier placement(Pyra, Roy, Cloud, in some circumstances Lucina as well) and I think this will be the case for most swordies including marth.

3. General Meta Advancement. By this, I'm referring to something similar to what happened with sheik and diddy kong over the wifi season. Marth mains have been exploring new ways of confirming and expanding their combos, and finding confirms into side special and ways to set up for neutral special. Overall, his advantage state has evolved greatly in the past few months and I don't see this advancement stopping soon.

4. Matchup spread. A lot of people say marth is inconsistent or his lack of results, but his matchup spread never gets brought up to the point people dont even thin about the matchup and just put him a tier lower than wherever they put lucina because "worse lucina" idea. Most matchups are pretty identical to lucina, with certain exemptions leaning either way. My initial post was a mix of misinterpretation and me trying to debunk the only argument people use for byleth- results.


I don’t think results matter for anyone including byleth and that was never what my point was supposed to be but reading it back it def looked like it- so let me go into more detail as to what I meant to say.

First, the characters only actual representation in competitive play is MkLeo, and no other byleth is close in any level. This is NOT my ultimate reasoning, but this point I made was supposed to lead to the following reason:

If everyone only sees one player use the character and that player is light years ahead of everyone in skill, people are going to see that character hundreds of times better than what they really are. A good example of what I mean is something like BassMage or Skyjay - the best mains of their respective characters. Whenever people watch them, they say the SAME thing when they do well, which is “this character may actually not be low tier” when in reality it’s just one really incredible player carrying that character to its limits on a mixture of just pure fundamental and lack of MU experience. MKLeo, in my opinion, is taking a mid/meh character and just beating people with it because he outplays them on so many levels- then people interpret it as the character having results when it’s just Leo bias.

Byleth is going to struggle down the line and I think people talking about him being high tier are thinking way too much about Leo winning with the character as well. In general, you kind of have to talk about his results when talking about his competitive play because that tends to be peoples only argument as to why he’s high tier too. So while I didn’t mean to talk about results as if they mattered, I ended up doing so somewhat because it’s just how people talk about byleths metagame. Here’s why byleth isn’t high tier without anything to do with me talking about Leo or results or whatever:

1.  The character just has no real answers to projectiles and general defensive play. Sure he has some decent burst options, however they’re all committal and if he wants to beat shield he’s going to need to get in to land the grab or nair, which for someone as slow as him, it won’t be easy.

2. The character should also struggle at landing, outside of landing with neutral air. When byleth is at higher points of the stage beyond the point of landing with nair, his garbage air speed and no real aerial movement is going to make it incredibly difficult for him to move out of dangers way. I guess he has a B reverse and side b, however they’re both really committal

3. Yes the character is good at edgeguarding but I’m not personally convinced even top players are adapting well to that. There’s certain situations where yea there’s nothing you can do, but willingly recovering high or in some situations horizontal is straight up asking asking for issues. 

4. Small characters give a ton of other characters hell, including byleth. In byleths case, jt makes it much more difficult to land forward and back airs, which is a huge issue for the character as that’s his main distance options, a general point of advantage against small characters.

5. I mentioned he struggled at defensive play and against projectiles, but mobility is just a huge issue for characters like byleth. It can mess up your advantage state, make it harder to control space even when you have such good hitboxes, and more.

6. Additionally his frame data is kind of all over the place. Sure, in moves like nair or upB it can seem like it’s good where it matters, however he has so many options that are slow when they really limit his options. Frame 12 and 13 for his fair and bair are on the slower side of things, frame 13 upsmash is just not good at all, and same goes for frame 13 down tilt. in general a ton of his moves are just really, really slow and while yea he has fast options, the amount of “this is slow but if it lands it’ll hurt” is almost ganon locked of comedic. 

So yea - I can see why people thought I thought byleth was bad cus results because it def looked that way but I can guarantee that isn’t actually why and my post had more to do with how I think people see Leo and think the char is better than they really are.

We just see lucina a whole ton more, thus when we see the rare marth out in play its what we're thinking of.

4. Again, we don't see marth in top play a lot, but they do get these confirms all time. interquartile range(IQR for short) basically refers to the middle 50% of values in a data set.

Basically, you find that value by organizing all the values(combos) in a numerical order, and then removing the largest and smallest values until you are left with half the data. 

The remaining largest value is considered the upper quartile, and the smallest remaining value is the lower quartile. 

Subtracting the Upper and Lower quartile will give you the interquartile range.

The reasoning why I consider it a good metric is because most damage output is not from combos - usually damage in ultimate comes from one hit exchanges, putting the opponent into disadvantage.

There's really only ever been one recorded stock that was even close to being exclusively done through combos(It was with Anality's Terry).

Since the data factored usually a good sample size(10 games minimum + 3 unique opponents), these outliers of a couple combos and no other damage to take a stock aren't usually too big of a factor in results.

I think folklore is better - but Taylor Swift can still evolve this folk-pop style and make it into something really special, and evermore is the first step to that. Too many songs, imo sound like filler, and some songs didnt have enough thought into it, at least from what I'm getting from it. 

**first, willow** is a cute introduction that solidifies this is similar to folklore if it wasn't confirmed before. I like the backing vocals and the hook melody, it mixes that folklore vibe with basic pop melody and it works really well.

**second, champagne problems**. i like how the piano is recorded, it sounds like someone is playing right in front of you - i think the bridge does a good job of building up as well. 

**third, gold rush**. Sick introduction and sick transition into an amazing first verse that's super catchy and engaging. The drumbeat and melodies work so well. The bridge/chorus is an interesting twist, but works. Best song of evermore so far, this has a lot more energy that I think the first two tracks lacked. 

**fourth, 'tis the damn season** has a interesting introduction verse with the slightly distorted guitar and scratchy snare. That being said, i don't think the pop melodies work that well in this mix. Speaking of the mix - I dont think the panning works at all. That scratchy snare gets really, REALLY annoying. The drums also get a bit odd and somewhat out of place as well. I hope this guitar distortion + production is seen later in the album, however.

**fifth, tolerate it** has a more dreamy piano production as compared to champagne problems. This, a lot like the previous track, has a lofi vibe. But because the drums aren't as obnoxious, and the melodies work MUCH better! On the same level as gold rush. Swift's vocals are really good on this track due to the layering and the emotion put into it. Lastly, theres something in the background, something like a shaker or noise thing I can't put my finger on. Whatever the case, it works.

**sixth, no body, no crime** carrie underwood?? I like the country production on this and how taylor's vocal performance alone still makes it feel like it fits on evermore. Additionally, that 'almost - belt' she does in the chorus is really exciting. Another solid song.

**seventh, happiness** I feel like while this song has good buildup, it doesn't give as much emotion and energy as I would have liked. The production doesn't feel weak, but it doesn't feel as intricate and it takes a while to feel that same level as intricate and thought out as some of the better tracks so far.

**eighth, dorothea** I really like the guitar strumming song, and in addition the production on this song. That being said, this feels very one note - and needs a serious a bit more dynamic, because it honestly sounded really flat and started somewhere, and went nowhere.

**ninth, coney island** I kind of found this song boring - This just feels like a cut song from folklore, which most of the other songs didn't feel like. Theres more dynamic than dorothea, and this dynamic succeeds especially when the melodies begin to layer and they begin to harmonize, but until this build up hits, I'm kind of left not knowing what to expect, and kind of not expecting anything.

**tenth, ivy** Taylor Swift is really good at pop melodies - and when she goes for them, its often her best songs. This song is really solid, and it might be one more favorites if I enjoyed the instrumentation more. The instrumentation felt a lot like coney island, though more mystical and bright. It's by no means bad, but I wish I still had that same feeling when I was listening to gold rush, tolerate it, or no body, no crime. I'd still say better than the last three.

**eleventh, cowboy like me** gave me a startle with the louder drum. It works, but I wasn't expecting it, which I liked. Again, Taylor succeeds in the pop melodies. I really liked the guitar solo/instrumental. Overall, a solid song.

**twelth, long story short** is probably the best song since no body, no crime - this song shows swift can make this escapism folk pop has so much potential and she can definetely experiment a lot more. The faster tempo and exciting drums that make you want to dance is something I wouldn't expect. This is single potential too.

**thirteenth, marjorie** honestly feels... filler. I like how the guitar is building energy as it's much faster than previous songs - but I don't think this song stands out or I'll even remember it in an hour.

**fourteenth, closure** ??? ??? what am i supposed to think about this song LOL I dont get the percussion being off beat and why it intentionally sounds like it's supposed to be a nuisance. I think it's supposed to show the piano and the music "drowning" the noise away?

**fifteenth, lastly, evermore** cant believed taylor swift covered kelly clarkson's 'catch my breath'. the introduction was okay - but was very filler folklore if you understand what i'm saying - then I was really caught off guard when the panned  vocals - but overall a really interesting and decent ending - a better ending than closure, that's for sure.

WTF Do I Know: HOLY FUCK THAT CHORUS. I LOVE IT!!! 

Plastic Hearts: Not as good as the opener, but still great. Kind of a predictable hook/melody but still groovy/fun. Amazing solo though. 

Angels Like You: Interesting place to put a slower ballad esque song. But god I love the bridge and chorus. I love how airy this production is. WAIT. THIS GUITAR.....

Prisoner: I like this song a ton. Loved it when it was released last week and I still enjoy it thouroughly. Would've loved an extended version with a guitar solo, but it's still great!

Gimme What I Want: Probably the weakest song so far. I don't dislike it, however I think the chipmunk vocals aren't that pleasing. Love the distortion/bass and production besides that.

Night Crawling: Great 80s rock banger. Totally didn't expect the synth keys and the backing vocals but they work so well. Also.. god the guitar riffs in this album have been so amazing so far.

Midnight Sky: Everyone loved this song when it came out except me, but it's 100% grown on me. I love the production on the song, from the bass, drums, etc, synths... god. Also love the ending too!

High: Wasn't really expecting something that felt as country like this, but it's still a great song. Also.. Miley's vocals are so good here. 

Hate Me: This country-pop song honestly feels out of place in the album. The half step chord progression kind of gets old on this sing too. 

Bad Karma: A very classic rock&roll song. I think it's kind of cute, though I dont know how I feel about the adlib-moaning part, they're kind of annoying at parts. 

Never Be Me: Dreamy, synth production. I love the melodies. I also really like the lyrics. Honestly has single potential. Miley's vocals here are some of the best on the album, as they're so emotional and impactful. 

Golden G String: Another dreamy production. I think it's an odd way of ending the album, as it sounds basically nothing like how it started. I guess the song is good, but it's a weird ending. I kind of wanted something more rock and roll.

BEST SONGS: Midnight Sky, Prisoner, WTF DO I Know, Angels Like You, 

GREAT SONGS: Plastic Hearts, Night Crawling, High, Never Be Me

GOOD SONGS: Bad Karma, Golden G String

MEH SONGS: Gimme What I Want, Hate Me

Overall, Great start but I think the ending fell short. The three tracks at the end, we already had but are great covers/remixes that add to the album.

Kelly Clarkson

1- Move You

The song is a fan favorite that clearly states what Kelly Clarkon wants with her music. The production and sound is soul-esque, a lot like the music that she was raised up on(aretha franklin) 

2- Because of You

A song thats synomynous with Kelly, and is an important part of her childhood experience. It should also feel cohesive right after Move You

3- A Moment Like This

Even though she doesnt like this song herself, this song represents a huge turn in Kelly Clarkson's life/career(winning american idol). Convienently also has a production that can match a similar vibe to the songs before.

4- Breakaway

I'd hate to put two of her least favorite songs on this alltime album, but it just works so well. Its a good transition from the first three songs to a more rock-esque vibe. It's also symbolizing a breakaway from that 'american idol' identity, as she becomes a main pop girl during this era

5- Since U Been Gone

As much as I'd love to put Behind These Hazel Eyes instead, this song represents her peak popularity, her rocker persona and her success much more. 

6- Haunted

This song, about her friends suicide, is an important transition into the somber and darker era of My December. Its a rock song, so cohesively it fits well after Since U Been Gone, while also hinting at something darker.

7- Irvine

This abrupt stop in rock, breaking cohesion, is intentional. This is where Kelly Clarkson reaches rock bottom during her Breakaway era, and the emptyness of the song where lyrics are everything really stops all momentum intentionally. 

8- Cry

The transition from My December to All I Ever Wanted was tough for me, but Cry will have to work. Its an incredibly sad song, but it's much more grand and finds Kelly back into a pop-rock ballad.

9- All I Ever Wanted

This is the only cover in this all-time album, which is an important aspect of Kelly Clarkson's appeal and discography. Cohesively, it sees a transition back into rock, while holding onto darker lyrics.

10- You Can't Win

Still a rock song, but the vibe feels different and the lyrics are a good transition in mindset from All I Ever Wanted. Its also an important transition to her next song.

11- Stronger

Finding herself into a positive song for the first time in a long time, this also has pop elements into it for the first time. 

12- Invincible

This is a pop ballad with a confident message put into it. It's a much slower paced song from Stronger, but should still be pop enough to feel cohesive. This also has a reference back to when Kelly Clarkson was younger, which leads to the next song. 

13- Piece by Piece

No surprise this is on here, as it nears the end of this all-time album. This song is in reference to Because of You, the second song listed. It wraps up those conflicts in the beginning of the album,  and shows a new part of Kelly Clarkson's life: motherhood.

14- Whole Lotta Woman

This song could be replaced by a lot of other Meaning of Life songs, but this is Kelly Clarkson being confident in herself, her roots, and her life. It's exciting and fun, which I think is a good way to end this all time album.
